title: A fresh bribery step
statement: Let $n\ge 2$, let $f$ be a monotone Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $J$ be a set of coordinates. Suppose the mean of the function obtained by setting every coordinate in $J$ to $+1$ lies in $[-99/100,99/100)$. Then some coordinate $i\notin J$ can be added to $J$ so that this mean increases by at least $199\log(n)/(1000000n)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The mean after setting coordinates in $J$ to $+1$ is at least $-99/100$
That mean is strictly less than $99/100$
